description: A guide to India's most important pilgrimage places across faiths: Hindu sites such as Varanasi, Tirumala, Vaishno Devi, the Char Dham and Jyotirlingas; the Golden Temple and Hemkund Sahib; Bodh Gaya and Sarnath; Palitana and Sammed Shikharji; Ajmer and Nizamuddin; Velankanni and Old Goa, with seasons, booking notes and how to choose.
dek: India's holy places span every major faith. This guide picks the sites most pilgrims plan their journeys around, and explains how to plan each.

intro: Pilgrimage is one of the main reasons Indians travel, and many of the country's busiest destinations are holy places: river towns such as Varanasi and Haridwar, hill shrines such as Tirumala and Vaishno Devi, the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Bodh Gaya, and the great Sufi dargahs.

This guide lists the places most pilgrims plan around, grouped by tradition, with the season and the booking or registration each one needs. It is a starting point; every site links to our detailed guide.
quickAnswer: Among India's most important pilgrimage places are Varanasi, Haridwar and Prayagraj on the Ganga; Tirumala (Tirupati), Vaishno Devi and the Char Dham; the twelve Jyotirlingas; Puri and Rameswaram; the Golden Temple in Amritsar; Bodh Gaya and Sarnath; Palitana and Sammed Shikharji; Ajmer Sharif; and Velankanni and the churches of Old Goa. Many need advance darshan booking or registration.
takeaways: Most pilgrims plan around a tradition: Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Sufi or Christian.
Tirumala, Vaishno Devi, the Char Dham and Amarnath need advance booking or registration on official portals.
Himalayan shrines open only in summer; the plains are best from October to March.
Festivals are spiritually special but bring the largest crowds.
Every temple, gurdwara, dargah and church has its own rules on dress and entry.

sections.heading: How to choose
list: Start with your tradition and any vow or ritual you want to complete.
Check the season: Himalayan shrines are summer-only; the south and the plains suit winter.
Check whether darshan booking or registration is needed, and book on the official site.
Allow buffer time: queues, weather and crowds make schedules unpredictable.
For older travellers, pick sites with road access or good assistance, and pace the trip.
after: Our pilgrimage planning guide goes through each step.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Book darshan, registration and helicopters only on official portals; fake sites are common.
Festivals and holidays bring the largest crowds; follow police and volunteer instructions.
High-altitude shrines need acclimatisation and medical advice for older pilgrims.
packing: Modest clothing, and a head covering for gurdwaras and dargahs
Basic medicines and a water bottle

faqs.q: Which is the most important pilgrimage place in India?
faqs.a: It depends on the tradition: Varanasi and the Char Dham for many Hindus, the Golden Temple for Sikhs, Bodh Gaya for Buddhists, and Palitana and Sammed Shikharji for Jains.

faqs.q: Which pilgrimage places need advance booking?
faqs.a: Tirumala darshan, Vaishno Devi and Amarnath registration, the Char Dham registration, and Kedarnath helicopters, among others.

faqs.q: When is the best time for pilgrimage in India?
faqs.a: October to March for most of the plains and the south; May to June and September to October for Himalayan shrines.

faqs.q: Can people of other faiths visit these places?
faqs.a: Most welcome all visitors who follow their rules, though some temples admit only Hindus; check before visiting.

faqs.q: Where should I go on my first pilgrimage?
faqs.a: Varanasi, Haridwar and Rishikesh make an easy first trip from north India; Tirumala, Madurai and Rameswaram from the south.
